operations.new: According to the family history, Hugh and [[McCullough-1964|Margaret McCullough]] married in 1733 and had three sons:

=== Record limits ===

The family history preserves a valuable account of Hugh's origins, occupation, marriage and sons, but was written long after the reported events. The parentage and dates in that account remain family tradition rather than independently proved relationships.<ref name="GlasgowHistory"/>

The collector sequence beside James McCullough makes one of the 1740 householders a useful working candidate for this Hugh. However, the return records no wife, children, age or townland for either Hugh, so the association alone does not establish identity. The second entry remains a separate namesake to investigate.<ref name="PHR1740"/><ref name="PHRSequence"/>

The 1772 notice establishes a Hugh Glasgow's presence in Tamlaght O'Crilly Parish; it does not distinguish this man from his younger son or another namesake. The two records support continued Glasgow presence in the district without proving which Hugh appears in both.<ref name="News1772"/>

=== Disambiguation: Contemporaries and Potential Conflation ===
Extreme caution is required when researching Barbara Glasgow in early 17th century Edinburgh and its surrounds, as several women shared this name. The Barbara Glasgow documented as mother to Catharine Little must be carefully distinguished from other known individuals, including:
operations.new: Do not merge this adult Barbara with [[Glasgow-3182|Barbara (Glasgow) Wilson]] or [[Glasgow-3302|Barbara (Glasgow) Johnson]] without continuity evidence. The latter is associated with George Johnstoun through a 21 November 1616 Edinburgh marriage<ref name="JohnstounMarriage1616">“Scotland, Marriages, 1561-1910”, database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYMH-HZJ : 11 February 2020), Barbara Glasgow in entry for George Johnstoun, 1616.</ref> and children including Daniell in 1617<ref name="Daniell1617">“Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950”, database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1YQ-BX4 : 16 September 2021), Barbara Glasgow in entry for Daniell Johnestoun, 1617.</ref> and Archebald in 1618.<ref name="Archebald1618">“Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950”, database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1Y3-2XL : 16 September 2021), Barbara Glasgow in entry for Archebald Johnstoun, 1618.</ref> A Barbara Glasgow married John Wilson in South Leith on 26 November 1611.<ref name="WilsonMarriage1611">“Scotland, Marriages, 1561-1910”, database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYML-ZBB : 11 February 2020), Barbara Glasgow in entry for John Wilson, 1611.</ref> These may concern the same woman or different contemporaries, but neither record establishes the mother of Catharine's identity. [[Glasgow-1102|Barbara Glasgow (1617-)]] is excluded by chronology.<ref name="Barbara1617">“Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950”, database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQC9-JYX : 12 February 2020), Barbara Glasgow, 1617.</ref>

operations.old:
* '''Barbara Glasgow, wife of George Johnstoun:''' (Likely [[Glasgow-3302|Barbara (Glasgow) Johnson (abt.1600–)]]). FamilySearch profile 9VM1-52D appears to '''conflate''' this woman's records with the mother of Catharine Little. Records associated with this Barbara include:
** Marriage to George Johnstoun on 21 November 1616 in Edinburgh Parish.<ref name="JohnstounMarriage1616">"Scotland, Marriages, 1561-1910", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYMH-HZJ : 11 February 2020), Barbara Glasgow in entry for George Johnstoun, 1616.</ref>
** Several children christened in Edinburgh Parish with George Johnstoun between 1617 and 1627, including Daniell (1617)<ref name="Daniell1617">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1YQ-BX4 : 16 September 2021), Barbara Glasgow in entry for Daniell Johnestoun, 1617.</ref> and Archebald (1618).<ref name="Archebald1618">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1Y3-2XL : 16 September 2021), Barbara Glasgow in entry for Archebald Johnstoun, 1618.</ref> (Other children mentioned in the source list for FS profile 9VM1-52D include Marione, Margaret, James, and Catharine Johnstoun).
** The estimated birth year of c. 1596 associated with FS profile 9VM1-52D fits this Barbara (wife of George Johnstoun) better than it fits the mother of Catharine Little.

* '''[[Glasgow-3182|Barbara (Glasgow) Wilson (abt.1590–)]]:''' Married [[Wilson-126696|John Wilson (1590–)]] on 26 November 1611 in South Leith Parish, Midlothian (adjacent to Edinburgh).<ref name="WilsonMarriage1611"> "Scotland, Marriages, 1561-1910," database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYML-ZBB : 11 February 2020), Barbara Glasgow in entry for John Wilson, 1611.</ref>

* '''[[Glasgow-1102|Barbara Glasgow (1617-)]]:''' Baptised 29 June 1617 in Edinburgh Parish, daughter of George Glasgow and Margaret Steuart.<ref name="Barbara1617">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQC9-JYX : 12 February 2020), Barbara Glasgow, 1617.</ref>

Given these contemporaries, it is crucial that further research confirms any additional records genuinely belong to the Barbara Glasgow who was mother to Catharine Little in 1611.

=== Research Notes ===

* '''Defining Record:''' This profile represents the Barbara Glasgow named as mother to Catharine Little, born 9 Sep 1611 and baptised 29 Sep 1611, daughter of Johne Little.<ref name="Catharine1611"/>
* '''Conflation Alert:''' FamilySearch profile 9VM1-52D appears to conflate this Barbara with Barbara Glasgow, wife of George Johnstoun (married 1616). Records require careful separation.
* '''Multiple Contemporaries:''' At least three, possibly four, women named Barbara Glasgow were living/marrying/having children in the Edinburgh/Leith area between 1610-1620, complicating identification.
* '''Conflicting Birth Estimates:''' The speculative birth estimate of c. 1586 fits better for the mother of Catharine Little (age ~25 in 1611). The FS profile estimate of c. 1596 fits better for the wife of George Johnstoun (age ~20 at marriage in 1616).
* '''Parentage & Origin Unknown:''' No sources confirming parents, specific origin, marriage, or death for Barbara (Glasgow) Little have been identified.

=== Current Larne reconstruction ===

John's Inishrush residence and his own family evidence remain distinct from the unresolved parentage of [[Glasgow-3902|Adam Glasgow]]. Their shared parish and the 1831 household list make a brother or other collateral relationship worth testing, but do not state one. The family Bible's naming pattern can suggest an older Adam and Maria as a research lead only; it cannot create or attach them. A broader Larne model makes [[Glasgow-1509|James Glasgow]] a possible earlier-generation candidate, but no record connects the ropemaker to John. The public Y-DNA comparison is useful for selecting descendants and testing a wider paternal network, but participant pedigrees and reported distances do not identify John's father or prove a specific relationship to Adam or Alexander. The best current conclusion is a documented Inishrush and Covenanter family with unproved collateral links to Adam and the Larne candidates.<ref name="JohnCurrent">The cited Bible, 1831 census and Y-DNA project results provide context, not a parental statement.</ref>

=== Inishrush and Drimbolg evidence ===

A separate McKeown family Bible records John Glasgow McKeown's birth at Inishrush on 17 April 1821 and baptism by the Rev. Joseph Orr. Drimbolg Reformed Presbyterian history records a John Glasgow in 1809 and as an elder in 1827. Together, these independent records substantially strengthen the identification of this John with the 1831 Inishrush householder, although neither names Adam as a relative.<ref name="McKeownBible">[https://www.hiltner.com/mckeown/getperson.php?personID=I1&tree=tree1 John Glasgow McKeown], family-Bible transcription and descendant page.</ref><ref name="Drimbolg">[https://www.oneirishrover.com/drimbolg-reformed-presbyterian-church/ Drimbolg Reformed Presbyterian Church], congregation history and session extracts.</ref>

The Guernsey County deed is the earliest secure Ohio evidence presently located for John; it establishes neither an Irish parent nor a sibling.<ref name="Deed1833Retained">[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-89WY-TFPB Guernsey County deeds, volume H, page 457].</ref>

operations.old: John Glasgow-867 and Samuel Glasgow-2908 belong to a specific '''father-John branch'''. John’s original 16 November 1846 marriage<ref name="Evidencef940c7acb4">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/view/?record_id=cima-3156063 original 16 November 1846 marriage].</ref> names his father as John Glasgow, farmer. The 1851 household expressly calls Samuel John’s brother. That chain directly establishes the brotherhood and names John-867’s father and his occupation. Extending that father statement to Samuel assumes they shared a father; the census does not distinguish full from half brothers. It does '''not''' identify that father with John Glasgow-1022, the older Glenleslie man, and it does not make Alexander another son. The younger John’s memorial says he died in 1895 aged 78, which implies a birth about 1816–17 and makes the candidate Glasgow-1022 less comfortable than an earlier census-age reading alone. Any maintained attachment to John-1022 is an uncertain identification of the father, not an additional record and not evidence for Alexander’s parentage.

=== Independent parentage tests, September 2026 ===

The ''Plattsburgh Sentinel'' reports Nancy Glasgow's death at Plattsburgh on 31 October 1891, aged about 75, and funeral at the Peristrome Presbyterian church. This corroborates her death date but conflicts with the approximate age in her January 1889 will: the sources imply birth about 1815–1816 or 1820–1821. The reconstructed sibling birth span therefore does not establish that their proposed father had two wives.<ref name="NancyDeathNotice1891">''Plattsburgh Sentinel'', 6 November 1891, p. 8, death notices; [https://www.nyshistoricnewspapers.org/?a=d&d=plts18911106-01.1.8 original newspaper page], image inspected 29 September 2026.</ref>

The Glenleslie daughter Nancy, reported in the 1851 return as dying in 1847 aged 36, is a different woman from Plattsburgh Nancy. A reconstruction placing both in John-1022's immediate family would require an unexplained second daughter of the same name or a revised sibling interpretation. This does not exclude every collateral or half-sibling connection.<ref>[https://durrushistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/10/1851irishcensusreturnscommadelimitedtextfilejul24_072.pdf 1851 Irish census returns transcription], Glenleslie, house 21, John Glasgow household and deaths since 1841; derived transcript, compared with maintained findings.</ref>

John Glasgow, farmer, named in John-867's 1846 marriage, remains the probable father; Alexander's own father is not directly named. An independent parent statement in another reconstructed sibling branch could test this without relying entirely on Nancy's petition. A Scottish marriage index names Mary Thomson, aged 37, marrying William Sneddon on 9 November 1860, with parents Robert Thomson and Mary Glasgon Thomson. The older extracted index places the marriage at Old Monkland, Lanarkshire.<ref>FamilySearch, ''Scotland, Marriages, 1561–1910'', [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XT1H-TBC Mary Thomson index], 1860, Old Monkland, Lanarkshire; inspected 29 September 2026. This indexes the same event as the civil-registration index.</ref> The mother is a candidate for the unidentified Mary Thompson branch, not an established match; the original image was not available for inspection.<ref>FamilySearch, ''Scotland, Civil Registration, 1855–1875, 1881, 1891'', [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:6TLK-6T1J Mary Thomson index], 9 November 1860; parents Robert Thomson and Mary Glasgon Thomson. Document reference 008056939_011_M9H1-8LK, image 32. Index inspected 29 September 2026; original restricted to a FamilySearch centre or affiliate library.</ref>

=== Working father connection ===

Robert and Samuel belong to the same documented sibling group as [[Glasgow-987|Thomas Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-3896|Daniel Glasgow]]. A descendant family account names [[Glasgow-3904|Alexander Glasgow of Lisnagaver]] as Thomas's father, and Thomas and Daniel are already attached to Alexander on that basis.<ref name="FatherTradition">Peter, “Trying to find Glasgow,” ''Genes Reunited'', [https://www.genesreunited.co.uk/boards/board/general_topics/thread/465937 discussion], descendant account naming Alexander and Rosanna as parents of Thomas Glasgow. This is family testimony rather than a contemporary parent record.</ref> Their proved brotherhood and compatible chronology support Alexander as an uncertain father of Robert and Samuel too. This connects the documented brothers through the existing family hypothesis; it does not make the father relationship certain. Rosanna's maternity is assessed separately and is not established by the sibling deeds.

=== New contemporary death notice and age conflict ===

The ''Plattsburgh Sentinel'' of 6 November 1891 reports that Nancy died '''at Plattsburgh on 31 October 1891, aged about 75''', and that her funeral took place on Monday afternoon at the '''Peristrome Presbyterian church'''. This independently corroborates the cemetery transcription's death date. Its age implies birth about 1815–1816, whereas Nancy's own January 1889 will, saying about 68, implies about 1820–1821. Both are approximate; the discrepancy is unresolved. The maintained census indexes also give varying ages (30 in 1860, 50 in 1870 and 65 in 1880), so the two estimates are not proved birth-year bounds.<ref name="NancyDeathNotice1891">''Plattsburgh Sentinel'', 6 November 1891, p. 8, death notices, Nancy Glasgow; [https://www.nyshistoricnewspapers.org/?a=d&d=plts18911106-01.1.8 original newspaper page], original image inspected 29 September 2026.</ref>

The original probate docket records a special guardian for minor heirs, a collateral inheritance tax appraisal commissioned from Cabell McLean in March 1894, and his report filed 28 April 1894. It does not reproduce a kinship schedule. Robert Wallace Anderson, son of Nancy's deceased nephew Robert, supplies a younger beneficiary who could explain a guardian, but the ward is not named in the docket.<ref name="NancyDocketReview1894">Clinton County Surrogate's Court, probate minutes, vol. 6, p. 6, Nancy Glasgow estate; FamilySearch DGS 005115656, image 34, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:33SQ-GYCZ-X98 original docket]; visually inspected 29 September 2026. Exact March day and guardian's name not confidently read.</ref>

=== Scottish indexed candidate, September 2026 ===

A Scottish marriage index records Mary Thomson, aged 37, marrying William Sneddon on 9 November 1860, with parents Robert Thomson and Mary Glasgon Thomson. The older extracted index places the marriage at Old Monkland, Lanarkshire. The mother is a candidate for this citation-defined Mary Thompson only: no Irish origin or Nancy relationship is established, and the original image was not inspected.<ref>FamilySearch, ''Scotland, Civil Registration, 1855–1875, 1881, 1891'', [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:6TLK-6T1J Mary Thomson bride index] and [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:6TLK-6T1K mother index]; 9 November 1860. [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XT1H-TBC Older extracted marriage index], Old Monkland, Lanarkshire. Both concern the same event. Indexes inspected 29 September 2026; original 008056939_011_M9H1-8LK, image 32, restricted to a FamilySearch centre or affiliate library.</ref>

On the reported ages, the Tannybrake widow mentioned above would have been about eight at the Scottish daughter's birth around 1823. The candidates should therefore be kept separate unless an age or identity correction is established. No spouse or child from the Scottish index is assigned here.

'''Mary Ellen Glasgow''' was born on 14 February 1867 at Lisnagaver, County Antrim, Ireland. Her mother was Mary Glasgow; no father was entered in the civil birth register. Ann Glasgow of Lisnagaver, who was present at the birth, informed the registration on 12 March 1867. The birth was registered in Dirraw district, Ballymoney union.<ref name="birth1867">General Register Office Ireland, births registered in 1867 in Dirraw district, Ballymoney union, County Antrim, printed page 6, entry 214, Mary Ellen; [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/birth_returns/births_1867/03501/2286677.pdf original register return, PDF page 1], [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/view?record_id=f66be225e5-6827480 IrishGenealogy record]; image inspected 30 September 2026.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Current evidence assessment ===

The GRONI birth index names Mary Glasgow and gives 17 February 1867 in the Ballymoney district, reference U/1867/31/1005/2/214.<ref>General Register Office for Northern Ireland (GRONI), civil birth index, Mary Glasgow, 17 February 1867, Ballymoney district, U/1867/31/1005/2/214; [https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/birth online index].</ref> The original return's entry 214 names Mary Ellen and clearly reads 14 February 1867.<ref name="birth1867" /> The matching district, year, numbered entry and February birth support identifying these as the same registration. The reason for the differing day in the index remains unresolved.

The mother may be [[Glasgow-3167|Mary Glasgow of Lisnagaver]], and the informant may be [[Glasgow-438|Ann Glasgow]], but these identifications require corroboration. The birth register does not state a relationship between the two women.<ref name="birth1867" />
